Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue ".NET 11 Release Candidate 1" (#444) at dotnet/announcements
Events.RelatedBody:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

# Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69806 – .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet-watch AspireServerService exposes information through the use of certain arguments, that in turn can enable code injection. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor); CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects Linux installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks) on Linux, you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-69806](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806) ### Acknowledgements Ky0toFu with Microsoft ### Revisions V1.0 (09/08/2026): Advisory published.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native can perform an out of bounds write while processing MSFZ PDB files. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/133438 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.10.0-beta1.24272.1, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 10 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 9 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET or Visual Studio. 2. If your application references Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, update the package reference to version 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 or later. Once you have installed the updated runtime, SDK, Visual Studio, or package, restart your apps for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-58649 – .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet watch BrowserRefreshServer does not adequately validate cross-origin WebSocket origins, potentially allowing IL and PDB information disclosure. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56166 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100, <= 9.0.119 | 9.0.120 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ### .NET 8 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100, <= 8.0.129 | 8.0.130 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400, <= 8.0.423 | 8.0.424 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. ### Describe the bug `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is a MSBuild item which Include value is not a file path. Should the SDK provide an ItemDefinitionGroup for this item type, with `Visible=false` metadata, so that IDEs can distinguish it from file items? ### Steps to reproduce 1. `dotnet new install Microsoft.NET.Runtime.WebAssembly.Templates.net10` 2. `dotnet new wasmbrowser` 3. Open project in Rider 4. Observe "JS" file visible in the project root ### Expected behavior Since `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is not a file item group, it's expected to be invisible by default. Or, at least, defined in default templates with Visible="false". ### Actual behavior Even though `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is not a file item group, it's still has default Visible=true. ### Is this a regression? No ### Are there any workarounds? There are two workarounds `Visible="false"` on each include: ```xml ``` Global `ItemDefinitionGroup`: ```xml false ``` ### dotnet --info output ```console .NET SDK: Version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 Commit: 3551975be0 Workload version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26460.1 MSBuild version: 18.11.0-1.26425.128+3551975be Runtime Environment: OS Name: Mac OS X OS Version: 27.0 OS Platform: Darwin RID: osx-arm64 Base Path: /usr/local/share/dotnet/sdk/11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 .NET workloads installed: [wasm-tools] Installation Source: SDK 11.0.100-rc.1 Manifest Version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128/11.0.100-rc.1 Manifest Path: /usr/local/share/dotnet/sdk-manifests/11.0.100-rc.1/microsoft.net.workload.mono.toolchain.current/11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128/WorkloadManifest.json Install Type: FileBased ``` ### IDE version JetBrains Rider 2026.2.1 ### Other details One can say it's not an SDK issue, but Rider issue. Because Rider decides to include all ItemGroups visible in the project tree, unless these are well known not-file includes. But MSBuild also has a `` feature allowing to globally predefine default metadata, without relying on specific tooling internal filtering.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 08:39 AM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

In my opinion the fix is easy: replace GetOutputPort by OutputPort in the call to

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Done.

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Razor source generator crashes on incomplete `@rendermode` attributes
Issues.Body:
### Description

The Razor source generator crashes while editing a component invocation with an incomplete `@rendermode` attribute. Roslyn reports CS8785 with an inner `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` instead of recovering from the incomplete Razor syntax.

Originally reported through Visual Studio Feedback as DevDiv work item 3065435, using Visual Studio 18.10.1.

### Reproduction

Create a Blazor component and reference another component with a minimised render mode attribute:

```razor
<Child @rendermode />
```

Supplying a valid render mode value does not crash.

### Actual behaviour

`RazorSourceGenerator` fails with CS8785. The inner exception originates in `ComponentRenderModeLoweringPass.ExecuteCore`, followed by `SourceGeneratorProjectEngine.ProcessRemaining` and Roslyn's incremental generator `TransformNode<T>.UpdateStateTable`.

`DefaultTagHelperResolutionPhase.ComponentTagHelperResolver` creates a `TagHelperDirectiveAttributeIntermediateNode` without value children for a minimised directive attribute. `ComponentRenderModeLoweringPass` then unconditionally reads `node.Children[0]`.

### Expected behaviour

Incomplete `@rendermode` syntax should follow the existing malformed-input recovery path and must not crash the source generator. Any normal parser or compiler diagnostics for the current edit state should still be reported.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Razor source generator crashes on incomplete `@rendermode` attributes" (#85692)

Issues.Title: Reduce Find in Files allocation
Issues.Body:
Find in Files Global Undo transiently opens many documents. Visual Studio currently serializes each full snapshot to Roslyn even though Roslyn's out-of-process LSP server already has that text in its synchronized workspace. This completes the server half of the existing textless `didOpen` handshake in [VSLanguageServerClient PR 782298](https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_git/VSLanguageServerClient/pullrequest/782298). The extension is negotiated only with Visual Studio. Other clients continue to send the full document text required by standard LSP.

Issues.Title: Hide StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern items by default
Issues.Body:
`StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` items use logical names such as `JS`, not file paths, but IDEs can still surface them as project tree entries. WebAssembly templates currently need explicit `Visible="false"` metadata to avoid showing these non-file items.

- **SDK defaults**
  - Added default `Visible=false` metadata for `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` in the Static Web Assets fingerprinting patterns props.
  - Applies to SDK-provided and project/template-defined fingerprint patterns unless explicitly overridden.

```xml
<ItemDefinitionGroup>
  <StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern>
    <Visible>false</Visible>
  </StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern>
</ItemDefinitionGroup>
```

- **Coverage**
  - Added a WebAssembly design-time evaluation test verifying a project-defined fingerprint pattern inherits `Visible=false`.

Issues.Title: `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` defined in WasmBrowser templates is visible in the project tree
Issues.Body: ### Describe the bug `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is a MSBuild item which Include value is not a file path. Should the SDK provide an ItemDefinitionGroup for this item type, with `Visible=false` metadata, so that IDEs can distinguish it from file items? ### Steps to reproduce 1. `dotnet new install Microsoft.NET.Runtime.WebAssembly.Templates.net10` 2. `dotnet new wasmbrowser` 3. Open project in Rider 4. Observe "JS" file visible in the project root ### Expected behavior Since `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is not a file item group, it's expected to be invisible by default. Or, at least, defined in default templates with Visible="false". ### Actual behavior Even though `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is not a file item group, it's still has default Visible=true. ### Is this a regression? No ### Are there any workarounds? There are two workarounds `Visible="false"` on each include: ```xml ``` Global `ItemDefinitionGroup`: ```xml false ``` ### dotnet --info output ```console .NET SDK: Version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 Commit: 3551975be0 Workload version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26460.1 MSBuild version: 18.11.0-1.26425.128+3551975be Runtime Environment: OS Name: Mac OS X OS Version: 27.0 OS Platform: Darwin RID: osx-arm64 Base Path: /usr/local/share/dotnet/sdk/11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 .NET workloads installed: [wasm-tools] Installation Source: SDK 11.0.100-rc.1 Manifest Version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128/11.0.100-rc.1 Manifest Path: /usr/local/share/dotnet/sdk-manifests/11.0.100-rc.1/microsoft.net.workload.mono.toolchain.current/11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128/WorkloadManifest.json Install Type: FileBased ``` ### IDE version JetBrains Rider 2026.2.1 ### Other details One can say it's not an SDK issue, but Rider issue. Because Rider decides to include all ItemGroups visible in the project tree, unless these are well known not-file includes. But MSBuild also has a `` feature allowing to globally predefine default metadata, without relying on specific tooling internal filtering.

Issues.Title: Add NativeAOT size and retention explorer
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- add dependency-free, hoverable SVG views of assembly-level NativeAOT size changes
- add an interactive assembly → namespace → type → member explorer for each platform
- inventory constructed generic types and generic method instantiations, including canonical `__Canon` forms
- show all direct retention callers, one shortest path from an AOT root, and large nodes with a single incoming dependency
- publish complete generic-instantiation and single-dependency CSVs beside the HTML report

The artifact index embeds each platform SVG in a collapsible `<details>` section and links its detailed explorer and CSVs. The PR comment links the downloadable artifact because GitHub strips interactive inline SVG from comments.

## Implementation

- uses the existing PowerShell/SizoScope assembly diff for compact change summaries
- independently reads the MIT-licensed MSTAT 2.x format with BCL APIs; no SizoScope source or AGPL dependency is copied into the SDK
- streams the full DGML graph instead of loading the approximately 783 MB file into memory
- passes `--scanfulllog` to ILC so incoming-dependency counts reflect the full retention graph
- handles multiple compiler graph records with the same formatted label by aggregating their incoming edges and selecting the shortest available root path

## Validation

- PowerShell treemap regression tests
- dependency-free synthetic MSTAT/DGML end-to-end self-tests, including duplicate DGML labels
- real `dotnet-aot` MSTAT plus full scan graph: 23,213,620 attributed bytes and 706,100 mapped incoming edges
- shell syntax and whitespace validation

## Preview

### Combined platform report

![NativeAOT size report overview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/598ecba6-afb1-465a-90ac-e1a68bd083ae)

### Assembly size diff

![NativeAOT platform size treemap](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bfdfaff-c0aa-47ab-ad1a-113a56c8e2c2)

### Member drilldown and retention analysis

![NativeAOT member-level size explorer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8e8e307-601f-4079-b8b1-8b020000ec61)

Issues.Title: dotnet format: support opt-in syntax-aware maximum line width
Issues.Body:
### Background

`dotnet format` honors `.editorconfig` whitespace and code-style preferences, but it has no syntax-aware maximum line-width setting. Existing `csharp_new_line_*` settings describe where specific constructs may break; they cannot decide whether to wrap based on the rendered line length.

This leaves projects that want a deterministic, SDK-native formatting workflow without a way to automatically reflow long C# method calls, constructors, fluent chains, object initializers, and similar expressions.

### Scenario

A project wants a simple, reproducible command:

```console
dotnet format
```

and an opt-in project setting that makes long code easier to review side-by-side, for example around 120 columns. The current alternative is to use a separate formatter such as CSharpier, which introduces a second formatting model and command into projects that otherwise rely on Roslyn and `.editorconfig`.

### Proposal

Add an **opt-in**, default-off maximum line-width policy to the C# formatting pipeline used by `dotnet format`.

The exact option name is intentionally left open for design discussion. An EditorConfig-style setting such as `csharp_format_max_line_length = 120` illustrates the intended project-level configuration.

The formatter should choose syntax-aware break points for expressions that can be represented on multiple lines, including method declarations and invocations, constructor calls, fluent chains, collection/object initializers, and conditional expressions.

### Expected behavior

Given an enabled target width, this:

```csharp
await service.ExecuteAsync(firstArgument, secondArgument, thirdArgument, cancellationToken);
```

could become:

```csharp
await service.ExecuteAsync(
    firstArgument,
    secondArgument,
    thirdArgument,
    cancellationToken
);
```

### Design considerations

- The policy should be disabled by default to preserve existing output and avoid broad formatting diffs.
- It should be deterministic and work with `--verify-no-changes` for CI.
- A soft target is likely more realistic than a strict limit: literals, URLs, directives, comments, generated code, and syntactically indivisible expressions may exceed it.
- It should not split string literals or comments in ways that can alter meaning or documentation formatting.
- The setting should coexist with existing `csharp_new_line_*` and indentation options.
- If the full formatter cannot reasonably support every syntax form initially, a documented supported subset would still be valuable.

### Why this belongs in `dotnet format`

This is not a request to replace the existing code-style analyzer model. It is a layout concern that would let SDK-only projects use one formatter command and one project configuration surface, instead of combining Roslyn-based style fixes with a separate opinionated re-printer solely for line-width reflow.

Issues.Title: Simplify CA1517 usage checks and expand regression coverage
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Follow up on dotnet/sdk#55898 with cleanup, additional tests, and a fix for a missed CA1517 suggestion. The original tuple-assignment fix is already merged; this main-only follow-up does not need a backport.

Remove the increment/decrement, ref/out argument, and writable-ref-initializer checks already covered by `GetValueUsageInfo(...).IsWrittenTo()`.

Allow read-only ref locals to use a `ReadOnlySpan<T>` parameter, matching the existing treatment of read-only ref returns. This intentionally enables a previously missed suggestion; users who elevate CA1517 to warning/error can see a new diagnostic. Writable ref locals remain excluded.

Preserve two remaining guards:

- Direct writable-ref variable declarators are not covered by the helper's initializer/declarator pattern.
- The existing ref-return guard checks the containing method, whereas `GetRefKind` selects the nearest anonymous or local function. Removing that guard changes existing behavior for reads captured by nested functions inside a ref-returning method.

Add nested-tuple and parenthesized-target write cases, plus an RHS-only tuple diagnostic/code-fix case, retaining the original swap and existing controls. Cover writable and read-only arguments, read-only ref locals and returns, and nested-function return-kind behavior.

Addresses the feedback in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55898#discussion_r3903272590, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55898#discussion_r3903249391, and https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56342#discussion_r4039042482.

## Validation

The focused `PreferReadOnlySpanOverSpanTests` suite passed 103/103 cases with no skips. The updated read-only-ref-local diagnostic/code-fix test failed before the fix because no diagnostic was produced, then passed with the fix. Existing writable-ref and read-only-return controls also pass.

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project src\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers\tests\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers.UnitTests\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers.UnitTests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PreferReadOnlySpanOverSpanTests" --skip-redist-check
```

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: Retarget SDK sources to net12.0 without updating stage zero
Issues.Body:
🤖 Separates source retargeting from the stage-0 SDK update, following [Viktor's suggestion](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/pull/9076#discussion_r4036205452). This keeps the net12 transition smaller while leaving both SDK version entries in `global.json` unchanged.

## Approach

- Set the SDK source TFM to `net12.0` and use Arcade's explicit `net11.0` targeting-pack baseline. The reference APIs and execution runtime remain on .NET 11 during this phase.
- Move SDK task/tool lookup paths and container API baselines to `net12.0`. Keep externally produced F# and WindowsDesktop tool paths on their actual packaged TFM, and preserve ApiCompat's lower compilation target.
- Separate the compiled SDK TFM from test-app defaults. Product branding, runtime dependencies, and template defaults are unchanged.
- Add task-layout regression coverage and document the source-only rollover phase.

## Temporary bootstrap accommodations

The pinned Arcade does not synthesize ASP.NET Core framework references, so a conditional baseline copy fills that gap. The older SDK also lacks net12 package-pruning data; `LoadPrunePackageDataFromNearestFramework` uses the baseline framework's data. Live Core and ASP.NET reference-pack overrides also recognize the explicit baseline version so net12 sources resolve against the flowed net11 packs, not the older stage-0 packs. These accommodations are scoped to the new source TFM, including platform-qualified variants, and the older bootstrap, and are documented for cleanup during the bootstrap transition.

## CI follow-up fixes

- Resolve watch tools using the SDK source TFM, and prevent a duplicate framework-provided DI abstractions assembly in the SDK layout. Aligning live reference packs fixes the telemetry logger's split assembly-identity failure.
- Build the verbosity test asset separately, then run `dotnet test --no-build -v ...`, so build output cannot split the VSTest result lines being asserted.
- Replace the multi-TFM test asset's process-module enumeration with active-run markers isolated to each test copy. This avoids the Windows `Win32Exception (299)` while preserving parallel-versus-sequential assertions. Update both consumers of the asset.
- Retry localization cleanup with the existing bounded IOException retry helper; persistent failures still propagate. The directory-lock failure also occurs on main (#56222; related proposal #56223). Its handle owner remains unidentified. Explicitly select the SDK under test for localization commands to avoid bootstrap/redist mixing during local runs.

## Validation

- Full Debug SDK build succeeded using the unchanged pinned stage-0 SDK, `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`; a fresh redist rebuild also succeeded after pack-alignment changes.
- Initial focused task-layout/library, Razor build, and Static Web Assets build/publish runs: 132 passed, 5 skipped.

Issues.Title: Improve container registry authentication consistency
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Aligns container publishing authentication with the configured registry endpoint and improves error reporting when processing redirected or retried requests.

- Applies consistent endpoint checks to authentication challenges and cached authorization headers.
- Uses the existing `CONTAINER1019` diagnostic for authentication challenges from an unexpected origin, including responses with incomplete or malformed parameters.
- Preserves authentication diagnostics through base-image retrieval and publication instead of replacing them with generic access or download errors.
- Avoids retrying blob downloads when authentication-response validation has already failed.

Related to https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/54225

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Prevent CA2263 from changing generic System.Type values
Issues.Body:
Backport of #55900 to release/11.0.1xx

Fixes #52654 and #53189

General RC2 backport approval has been obtained. This backports the final merged patch, which retains broader generic-overload matching rather than the earlier proposed narrowed patch. Confirm that scope and its diagnostic impact when recording `servicing-approved` on this PR.

## Customer Impact

- [x] Customer reported
- [ ] Found internally

CA2263 can recommend a generic overload when `typeof(Type)` is ordinary data rather than a runtime type selector. Applying the fixer can turn `ImmutableHashSet.Create(typeof(Type))` into an empty `ImmutableHashSet.Create<Type>()`. It can also drop expanded `params`/VB `ParamArray` arguments, silently changing behavior while leaving compilable code.

The fix distinguishes declared `System.Type` selectors from data and preserves non-selector source arguments and their trivia. Additional compatibility checks preserve omitted optional defaults and expanded-array semantics.

## Regression

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

These reported defects have prior-release exposure; a previously working release boundary has not been established. They are existing analyzer/code-fixer correctness defects, not new .NET 11 behavior.

## Testing

Includes C#/VB coverage for Type-as-data false positives, expanded and explicit argument arrays, optional defaults (including signed zero and decimal representation), argument trivia, fixed-argument to generic-params matching, and positive/negative expression-statement and consumed-result cases.

The final source diff and included test cases were inspected, and the backport workflow completed successfully. Release-branch test results remain pending; successful backport creation does not establish test execution.

## Risk

This is not solely a false-positive removal. The merged patch retains broader generic-overload matching and shared invocation reconstruction used by both diagnostic validation and the fixer. It can surface additional suggestions; users who elevate CA2263 to warning/error can therefore encounter new build diagnostics. Default severity and enablement are unchanged.

The patch adds checks for optional-default compatibility, preserves synthesized array types for expanded arguments, and restores positive/negative expression-statement coverage. Release sign-off should account for the final scope and newly diagnosed overload shapes, rather than relying on the earlier narrowed-patch assessment.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Fix spurious CA1416 warnings in guard members and in nameof
Issues.Body:
Backport of #56042 to release/11.0.1xx

Fixes #54066

RC2 backport approval has been obtained; `servicing-approved` still needs to be recorded on this PR.

## Customer Impact

- [x] Customer reported
- [ ] Found internally

CA1416 reports false platform-compatibility warnings inside valid platform guard helpers because their bodies lose the assembly's supported-OS context. It also reports warnings for compile-time `nameof`/`NameOf` references that do not access the API. The Microsoft Store report describes dozens of false positives. CA1416 is enabled as a warning by default, so affected warnings-as-errors builds can fail.

The backport restores assembly-level context in guard bodies and excludes name-only references. The name-only correction also applies to CA1422.

## Regression

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

These are existing analyzer correctness defects that predate .NET 11. A previously working release boundary has not been established for these reports; this is not presented as a new .NET 11 regression.

## Testing

Includes supported- and unsupported-platform guard cases for assembly-context preservation and a containing-type negative control. Includes C#/VB name-only references with real API-access controls, plus CA1422 obsolete-platform name coverage. The final source diff and included tests were inspected. The main PR reports that the regressions were reproduced before the fix and the full analyzer test suite passed; this is the source PR's reported result, not a new release-branch run.

The backport workflow completed successfully. Release-branch test results remain pending.

## Risk

The production change is confined to the platform analyzer; it does not change shared dataflow or default severities. Guard bodies recover only assembly-level requirements, not containing-type requirements, preserving warnings for genuinely unsupported accesses. Compile-time name references no longer warn under CA1416/CA1422, while actual API references remain analyzed. Negative controls cover these distinctions.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Prevent CA2025 analyzer crash for direct field arguments
Issues.Body:
Backport of #55904 to release/11.0.1xx

Fixes #53926

RC2 backport approval has been obtained; `servicing-approved` still needs to be recorded on this PR.

## Customer Impact

- [x] Customer reported
- [ ] Found internally

When CA2025 is enabled, passing a non-local disposable argument to a task-returning invocation, awaiting the task later, and analyzing disposal in the same method can crash the analyzer with `NullReferenceException`/`AD0001`. This interrupts analysis and can fail warnings-as-errors builds. The backport removes the analyzer crash; it does not address an application crash or enable this opt-in rule.

## Regression

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

The issue investigation reports reproduction with .NET 10 and .NET 11, with .NET 9 as a negative control. This is an existing prior-release regression, not a newly introduced .NET 11 rule.

## Testing

Includes `NonLocalArgumentsAwaitedElsewhereBeforeDispose_NoDiagnosticAsync`, covering field, property, and method-result arguments in both C# and Visual Basic, followed by delayed awaits and disposal. The final source diff and included coverage were inspected; the backport workflow completed successfully. Release-branch test results remain pending and are not implied by successful backport creation.

## Risk

Low. The change filters null entries from the existing local-reference extraction helper. Converted and unconverted local references retain their existing handling. Non-local arguments were already unsupported by this tracking path; filtering them removes the exception rather than removing working field/property analysis. No diagnostic severity, default enablement, or new field-analysis support is introduced.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Fix CA1517 false positive for tuple assignments
Issues.Body:
Backport of #55898 to release/11.0.1xx

Fixes #53388

RC2 backport approval has been obtained; `servicing-approved` still needs to be recorded on this PR.

## Customer Impact

- [x] Customer reported
- [ ] Found internally

CA1517 recommends changing `Span<T>` to `ReadOnlySpan<T>` even when elements are modified through tuple/deconstruction assignment, such as `(values[x], values[y]) = (values[y], values[x])`. Applying that recommendation makes the writes fail compilation. Customers who elevate the suggestion to warning/error can also encounter build-blocking false positives without applying the fix.

## Regression

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

CA1517 is new in .NET 11. Its direct-parent assignment check misses indexer writes nested inside a tuple assignment, producing an invalid recommendation for existing writable code.

## Testing

Includes `SpanParameter_WrittenViaTupleAssignment_NoDiagnostic`, covering a tuple swap of `Span<char>` elements. The source diff and included regression test were inspected; the backport workflow completed successfully. Release-branch test results remain pending and are not implied by successful backport creation.

## Risk

Low. One production-line change reuses the existing `GetValueUsageInfo(...).IsWrittenTo()` helper to recognize writes. It removes invalid read-only recommendations rather than expanding diagnostic applicability. The rule remains a suggestion by default; no severity or enablement changes are included.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

We investigated building a somewhat dynamic pipeline for a mono-repo, to keep PR-pipeline times short.
Until the 'affected-test' solution is implemented though, we thought a combination of pre-generated yaml + pipeline self-checks would work.
however using the project name for `--publish-azdo-run-name` breaks the call.

### Steps to reproduce

  </ItemGroup>

dotnet test --project TestProject2.csproj --no-build -- --report-azdo --publish-azdo-test-results --publish-azdo-run-name TestProject2.csproj --retry-failed-tests 3

fatal error and exit

i don't know. We've only been recently able to use `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.AzureDevOpsReport` due to a bug, and our pipelines having been vstest based up until now

avoid ".sln" / ".csproj" in the `--publish-azdo-run-name` parameter

{

}

Issues.Title: `dotnet new search` throws RevocationStatusUnknown when using TLS inspection proxy (macOS)

Hi there!

Recently my organization enabled TLS inspection proxy for macOS clients and since then I wasn't able to use `dotnet new search` command. It throws `RevocationStatusUnknown` when trying to establish a TLS connection.

Issues.Title: NativeAOT Cross-Compilation Support for macOS and Windows
Issues.Body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, NativeAOT builds must be performed on platform-specific build hosts — macOS targets require a macOS builder, and Windows targets require a Windows builder. This adds significant overhead to CI/CD pipelines, as teams must provision and maintain separate build infrastructure for each target platform.



### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like the ability to perform NativeAOT cross-compilation from a **Linux builder host** targeting **macOS** and **Windows** outputs. This would allow teams to consolidate their build infrastructure onto Linux hosts while still producing native AOT-compiled binaries for all three platforms.

Specifically:
- `dotnet publish -r osx-x64 `with NativeAOT from a Linux host
- `dotnet publish -r osx-arm64` with NativeAOT from a Linux host
- `dotnet publish -r win-x64` with NativeAOT from a Linux host
- `dotnet publish -r win-arm64` with NativeAOT from a Linux host

This would reduce build infrastructure complexity, lower costs, and simplify CI/CD pipelines — especially for teams that already standardize on Linux-based build environments.

### Alternatives you've considered

- **Maintaining platform-specific build hosts** — This is the current approach. It works but requires provisioning and maintaining separate macOS and Windows build agents, which increases infrastructure cost and CI/CD pipeline complexity.
- **Using platform-specific CI/CD stages** — Running dedicated macOS and Windows stages in the pipeline solely for the NativeAOT publish step. This adds pipeline latency and cross-stage artifact management overhead for what is fundamentally a compilation task.
- **IL trimmed / ReadyToRun as a fallback** — Publishing with PublishReadyToRun or PublishTrimmed instead of NativeAOT. These do support cross-compilation, but sacrifice the startup performance, memory footprint, and single-file deployment benefits that NativeAOT provides.
- **Docker / VM-based cross-compilation** — Running macOS or Windows VMs or containers on Linux hosts to simulate native builds. This is fragile, has licensing constraints (especially for macOS), and negates the simplicity benefits of true cross-compilation support.


### Additional context

- **Real-world use case:** We build and ship a cross-platform endpoint agent (targeting Windows, macOS, and Ubuntu) from a centralized CI/CD pipeline. Today, we are forced to maintain three separate platform-specific build hosts just for the NativeAOT compilation step. Everything else in our pipeline — restore, test, static analysis — runs on Linux. The NativeAOT step is the sole reason we need macOS and Windows build infrastructure.
- **Scale impact:** For organizations managing large fleets of cross-platform agents or CLI tools, this multiplies across every repo and every build pipeline. Consolidating onto Linux builders would significantly reduce operational overhead.
- Precedent: Go, Rust, and Zig all support cross-compilation to macOS and Windows from Linux out of the box. This is an increasingly expected capability for modern compiled languages and a common reason teams choose those ecosystems over .NET for cross-platform CLI/agent workloads.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "NativeAOT Cross-Compilation Support for macOS and Windows" (#56333)

Issues.Title: Plumb CancellationToken through all CLI commands for consistent Ctrl+C/SIGTERM behavior
Issues.Body:
`CommandBase.Execute()` had no way to observe cancellation, so `Ctrl+C`/SIGTERM was not handled consistently across `dotnet` CLI commands. System.CommandLine's `Func<ParseResult, CancellationToken, Task<int>>` `SetAction` overload provides a token, but it wasn't wired through the command tree.

## Core change
- `CommandBase.Execute()` → `Execute(CancellationToken cancellationToken)` (abstract), updated across all ~47 command implementations.
- Added `CommandExtensions.SetAction(Func<ParseResult, CancellationToken, int>)` in `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.CommandLine` so synchronous command handlers can register with System.CommandLine's cancellable action pipeline without repeating `Task.FromResult` boilerplate at every call site:

```csharp
command.SetAction((parseResult, cancellationToken) =>
    new WorkloadInstallCommand(parseResult).Execute(cancellationToken));
```

## Threading the token through call chains
- Propagated `CancellationToken` through internal call chains for Tool, Workload, Restore, Package, Run, Publish, Build, Pack, Store, Clean, MSBuild, and Sdk Check commands.
- `RunApiCommand` now reads stdin via `Console.In.ReadLineAsync(cancellationToken)` instead of blocking `Console.ReadLine()`, and exits its loop gracefully if the read is cancelled — this makes cancellation actually interrupt a pending stdin read rather than waiting for the next line.

## Scope boundaries (intentionally left as-is)
- `AotRunCommand.cs` (`#if CLI_AOT`) is out of scope for this managed-CLI-focused pass.
- Deep internal MTP test-build helpers (`MSBuildUtility.cs`) and the `dotnet new` post-action callback boundary (`DotnetCommandCallbacks.cs`) use `CancellationToken.None`/`default`, since no cancellation token currently flows into those subsystems.

## Tests
- Updated `WorkloadCommandParser`'s `executeUpdate` delegate shape and corresponding `GivenDotnetWorkloadUpdate.cs` tests.
- Updated `CommandBase`-derived `.Execute()` call sites across test files to pass `CancellationToken.None`, leaving unrelated test-infrastructure `.Execute()` calls (e.g. `DotnetCommand`, `DotnetNewCommand` process runners) untouched.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #56331

Issues.Title: Plumb cancellationtokens through all CLI commands for consistent behavior
Issues.Body:
A good follow-up might be to make async commands more first-class in the .NET CLI / in `CommandBase`. As far as I can tell, I don't think the synchronous version of `ToolExecuteCommand.Execute()` is called from anywhere.

_Originally posted by @lbussell in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55958#pullrequestreview-5227033032_

The `Func<ParseResult, CancellationToken, Task<int>>` overload of System.CommandLine's `SetAction` provides the cancellation token, and we can plumb that through every Command we create so that a `Ctrl+C`/SIGTERM is handled correctly.

Issues.Title: .NET 11 Release Candidate 1
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Body: # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new).
